title: Keyed lists that keep row identity
summary: Reconcile a product list by id, then review a component that renders with map and loses row identity.

scenario.briefing: The product list keeps input state on the wrong row after a filter change. The team suspects the list is matched by position instead of product id.

objectives.description: Review a list for identity and prop-binding risks.

hints: Build a map from the current rows keyed by id.
Walk the next rows and look each id up in that map.
Reuse the existing object when the id matches and count it.
Return the new array plus the reuse count.

misconceptions.testDescription: Rows are matched by id when the order changes.
misconceptions.feedback: Position is not identity. When the array is reordered, an index match moves the old state onto a different product.

misconceptions.description: Rebuilding every row on each update.
misconceptions.testDescription: Rows with the same id are reused.
misconceptions.feedback: Rebuilding discards row-local state and defeats fine-grained updates. Reuse the object when the id is unchanged.

misconceptions.description: Treating map rendering as an acceptable keyed list.
misconceptions.feedback: Map plus an index key recreates rows and loses identity. Block the change until the list renders from a stable key.

sections.title: Identity is not position
sections.body: A list row is the same row when its id is the same, even if it moved. Reconciling by id preserves the row's DOM and state; reconciling by index swaps content between nodes.

sections.title: For tracks keyed rows
sections.body: Solid's For component reconciles a list by item identity. Mapping the array yourself rebuilds every row on each change and discards local state.

sections.title: Reuse is observable
sections.body: A reconciler can report how many rows it reused. That number exposes whether the implementation matched by id or simply rebuilt the array.

steps.title: Review the product list
steps.prompt: Review ProductList.tsx and select every real identity or reactivity problem.
hints: Check whether the list uses For or a plain map.
Look at the value used as the row key.
Check whether products is read through the live props object.
Reject findings that describe code the artifact does not contain.

artifact.title: ProductList.tsx
artifact.caption: The component destructures props, renders with map, and uses the array index as the row key.

findings.label: The list renders with map instead of For, so rows are rebuilt rather than reconciled by id.
The map callback uses the array index as row identity.
The props object is destructured, so later parent updates never reach this component.
The list already uses For to reconcile rows by id.
The filter expression is wrapped in createMemo, so query changes do not rerun it.

verdicts.label: Block the change until the listed risks are fixed.
Ship it; the remaining concerns are cosmetic.
Only formatting and naming need work.

steps.explanation: The list uses map with an index key, so reordering moves rows to new identities. Destructuring props also snapshots the initial array, so parent updates never arrive. There is no For and no createMemo in the artifact.
